details:
* SECURITY UPDATE: Memory amplification denial of service in the DTLS
     record layer: buffering a record that arrives early for the next epoch
     retained the entire read buffer, sized for the largest possible DTLS
     record (~16.7KB), rather than only the record's own bytes, so a peer
     sending a stream of small forged next-epoch records could make an
     endpoint retain around 1.7MB per connection.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-54874.patch: copy only the record's on-wire
       bytes into the queue entry and rebase the record pointers on
       retrieval in ssl/record/rec_layer_d1.c, ssl/record/record.h,
       ssl/record/record_local.h and ssl/record/ssl3_record.c, and lower
       the unprocessed_rcds queue limit to 16.
     - CVE-2026-54874
   * SECURITY UPDATE: Out-of-bounds heap write in CMS decryption: the
     key-unwrap output buffer was sized from the cipher's length query, but
     the AES-WRAP-PAD unwrap primitive writes and cleanses up to inlen bytes
     on its integrity-failure paths, so a crafted CMS message naming a
     padded key-wrap OID caused an 8-byte write past the allocation.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-63072.patch: size the unwrap output buffer
       for the worst case in cms_kek_cipher() in crypto/cms/cms_kari.c.
     - CVE-2026-63072
